container_info.description:
The Knowledge Bot is an AI-powered chatbot system designed to answer user queries based on a curated context of sample questions and answers. The system features a modern web-based interface, robust backend integration with Google Gemini for live AI responses, and comprehensive error handling and logging. It is intended to provide authoritative, context-aware answers for software testing and related domains, supporting both end users and internal teams.

Key features include:
- Modern chat UI for seamless user interaction
- Real-time AI-powered responses using Google Gemini
- Context injection from curated Q&A datasets
- RESTful API endpoints for chat and answer retrieval
- Comprehensive error handling, logging, and monitoring
- Responsive design and accessibility compliance
- Secure integration and privacy controls
- OpenAPI documentation for backend endpoints
- Scalable architecture for future enhancements
container_info.reasoning: The container is labeled 'frontend' and the application describes a modern web-based chat UI (SPA-like) for real-time AI responses. The Dockerfile summary includes frontend toolchains and CLIs such as nodejs, npm, yarn, typescript, create-react-app, @vue/cli and @angular/cli. Given the prevalence of React tooling (create-react-app present) and React's suitability for interactive chat UIs, React is the most appropriate choice for this frontend container.
requirements: nodejs (already present) and npm or yarn for package management
create-react-app or minimal React project files (package.json, src/, public/)
react and react-dom dependencies (minimal versions) and optionally typescript if using TS
a lightweight dev server: react-scripts (from create-react-app) or vite for faster builds
build-essential already present for native modules if needed
headless environment variables configured (e.g., PORT, NODE_ENV=development)
simple start script in package.json to run the dev server (e.g., npm run start)
basic liveness endpoint served by the dev server (optional) for container checks
minimal test harness: jest (already available) with one lightweight smoke test
no production web servers (nginx) or heavy monitoring/logging — use development server only

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Persist neutral headless environment variables and ensure Node/npm presence. Writes /etc/profile.d/frontend_headless.sh with PORT, BROWSER=none, CI=true and conditionally prepends npm global bin if present. Verifies node and npm versions (Node major >=18) and ensures the workspace directory exists. This ensures headless behavior and PATH persistence for future shells.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/knowledge-bot-f38ec8c2/Frontend"
# compute npm global bin if available
NG_BIN="$(command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 && npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || true)"
sudo bash -c 'cat >/etc/profile.d/frontend_headless.sh <<"EOF"
# frontend headless defaults
export PORT=3000
export BROWSER=none
export CI=true
# npm global bin placeholder (replaced at runtime if present)
if [ -n "${NG_BIN_PLACEHOLDER}" ] && [ -d "${NG_BIN_PLACEHOLDER}" ]; then
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *:"${NG_BIN_PLACEHOLDER}":*) :;;
    *) export PATH="${NG_BIN_PLACEHOLDER}:$PATH";;
  esac
fi
EOF
' && sudo chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/frontend_headless.sh
if [ -n "$NG_BIN" ]; then sudo sed -i.bak "s|\${NG_BIN_PLACEHOLDER}|$NG_BIN|g" /etc/profile.d/frontend_headless.sh && sudo rm -f /etc/profile.d/frontend_headless.sh.bak; else sudo sed -i.bak '/NG_BIN_PLACEHOLDER/,+3d' /etc/profile.d/frontend_headless.sh || true; sudo rm -f /etc/profile.d/frontend_headless.sh.bak || true; fi
# workspace and tool validation
mkdir -p "$WS"
command -v node >/dev/null || (echo "ERROR: node not found" >&2; exit 3)
command -v npm >/dev/null || (echo "ERROR: npm not found" >&2; exit 4)
NODE_V=$(node -v | sed 's/^v//')
NODE_MAJOR=$(echo "$NODE_V" | cut -d. -f1)
if [ "${NODE_MAJOR:-0}" -lt 18 ]; then echo "ERROR: Node >=18 required, found $NODE_V" >&2; exit 5; fi
echo "node: $(node -v)"; echo "npm: $(npm -v)"

steps.name: build_project
steps.description: Validation/build step that ensures a build script exists and performs an automated, idempotent remediation if it does not. If package.json lacks a "build" script, the step will add or patch a minimal CRA-compatible package.json (keeping existing fields), install dependencies non-interactively (npm ci when possible), run npm run build with NODE_ENV=production, validate build/ artifacts, and emit concise diagnostics on failure. This resolves the prior blocking error when no build script was present.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/knowledge-bot-f38ec8c2/Frontend"
cd "$WS"
# ensure package.json exists; if missing create minimal CRA-compatible one
if [ ! -f package.json ]; then
  cat >package.json <<'JSON'
{
  "name": "frontend",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "private": true,
  "engines": {"node": ">=18"},
  "scripts": {"start":"react-scripts start","build":"react-scripts build","test":"react-scripts test"},
  "dependencies": {"react":"^18.2.0","react-dom":"^18.2.0","react-scripts":"^5.0.1"}
}
JSON
fi
# if package.json exists but lacks a build script, patch it idempotently
if ! node -e "const fs=require('fs');const p=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json')) ; process.exit(p.scripts && p.scripts.build ? 0 : 1)" 2>/dev/null; then
  # create a temp modified package.json that preserves existing fields and injects scripts/deps if missing
  node -e "const fs=require('fs');let p=fs.existsSync('package.json')?JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('package.json')):{};p.scripts=p.scripts||{};p.scripts.start=p.scripts.start||'react-scripts start';p.scripts.build=p.scripts.build||'react-scripts build';p.scripts.test=p.scripts.test||'react-scripts test';p.dependencies=p.dependencies||{};p.dependencies['react']=p.dependencies['react']||'^18.2.0';p.dependencies['react-dom']=p.dependencies['react-dom']||'^18.2.0';p.dependencies['react-scripts']=p.dependencies['react-scripts']||'^5.0.1';fs.writeFileSync('package.json',JSON.stringify(p,null,2));console.log('patched package.json to include build/start/test and minimal deps');"
fi
# install dependencies deterministically
if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
  npm ci --no-audit --no-fund || (echo "ERROR: npm ci failed" >&2; tail -n 200 /home/kavia/.npm/_logs/*-debug-0.log 2>/dev/null || true; exit 4)
else
  npm i --no-audit --no-fund || (echo "ERROR: npm i failed" >&2; tail -n 200 /home/kavia/.npm/_logs/*-debug-0.log 2>/dev/null || true; exit 5)
fi
# run production build and validate artifacts
export NODE_ENV=production
npm run build || (echo "ERROR: npm run build failed" >&2; tail -n 200 /home/kavia/.npm/_logs/*-debug-0.log 2>/dev/null || true; exit 6)
if [ ! -d build ]; then echo "ERROR: build failed - build/ missing" >&2; exit 7; fi
du -sh build || true

steps.name: validate_devserver_readiness
steps.description: Start the dev server (npm run start) headlessly with NODE_ENV=development, wait for readiness by probing http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/index.html and scanning logs for compile markers, capture evidence (HTTP code and HTML snippet and logs), then stop the server cleanly and ensure no orphaned processes remain. Depends on environment, scaffold, deps, test, and build steps to ensure full validation.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WS="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/knowledge-bot-f38ec8c2/Frontend"
cd "$WS"
PORT=${PORT:-3000}
export NODE_ENV=development
export CI=true
export BROWSER=none
LOGFILE=$(mktemp -t frontend-dev-logs.XXXX)
# start dev server headlessly and capture logs; record PID
setsid env PORT="$PORT" NODE_ENV="$NODE_ENV" BROWSER=none CI=true npm run start >"$LOGFILE" 2>&1 &
PID=$!
sleep 1
READY=0
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  sleep 1
  HTTP=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/index.html" || echo "000")
  if [ "$HTTP" = "200" ]; then READY=1; break; fi
  if grep -q -E "Compiled successfully|Compiled with warnings|You can now view" "$LOGFILE" 2>/dev/null; then READY=1; break; fi
done
STATUS_CODE=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/index.html" || echo "000")
SNIPPET=$(curl -sS "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/index.html" | head -c 512 || true)
echo "EVIDENCE: HTTP_STATUS=$STATUS_CODE"
echo "EVIDENCE_SNIPPET=${SNIPPET}"
echo "--- DEVSERVER LOG (tail) ---"
tail -n 200 "$LOGFILE" || true
# attempt graceful shutdown
kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || sudo kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 1
LEFTOVER_PIDS=$(pgrep -f "react-scripts|node .*react-scripts" || true)
if [ -n "$LEFTOVER_PIDS" ]; then
  sudo kill -TERM $LEFTOVER_PIDS 2>/dev/null || true
  sleep 1
  sudo kill -KILL $LEFTOVER_PIDS 2>/dev/null || true
fi
wait "$PID" 2>/dev/null || true
cp "$LOGFILE" /tmp/frontend-dev-logs.last 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$LOGFILE"
if [ "$READY" -ne 1 ]; then echo "ERROR: dev server did not become ready" >&2; echo "Log copied to /tmp/frontend-dev-logs.last"; exit 6; fi

(3) Modified deps-001 to avoid --silent on failures, emit node/npm versions after successful install, and check for package-lock/package.json timestamp mismatches to prefer npm ci when appropriate. (4) Updated test-001 to export CI=true and NODE_ENV=test locally (not globally), run tests deterministically via 'npm test -- --watchAll=false --runInBand', and keep a lightweight smoke test. (5) Kept build-001 to run a production build but clarified its category and added safety checks; build remains a separate step. (6) Rewrote validation-001 to remove implicit dependency on build step (validation still depends on build per policy but start no longer requires build artifacts), start dev server and track direct PID, kill PID gracefully (sudo if needed), verify termination, probe HTTP /index.html for readiness and also check logs for common compile messages, and preserve short-lived logs for diagnostics. These changes modify env-001, scaffold-001, deps-001, test-001, build-001, validation-001 to resolve the feedback about environment persistence safety, process termination privileges, redundant build-before-devserver, logging verbosity, and test invocation determinism.

Refined build_project (build-001) to resolve the engineer's blocking issue: when package.json lacks a build script, the build step now idempotently injects a minimal CRA-compatible package.json (or patches existing package.json to add a "build" script), installs dependencies non-interactively (npm ci when lockfile exists else npm i), runs npm run build, validates build/ artifact presence and size, and emits concise logs on failure. Preserved other steps (env-001, scaffold-001, deps-001, test-001, validation-001) but ensured build-001 now performs automated remediation to unblock the build. Reason: the engineer reported a critical failure due to missing "build" script; automated, idempotent remediation within build-001 addresses this without requiring manual architect input.
